# A component built at run time may name a prop with a word the target's
# language reserves. A call site binds a prop by name, so passReservedNames
# leaves it as written, and html's factory bound each prop as a local of its
# own name: `let default = props.default;`, which esbuild refused, so a page
# holding settings.kept under a `for` did not build. A prop JavaScript
# reserves is a local of another spelling now (javascript.SafeIdent).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var log list[string] = []

component field(label string, default string) ui.node {
    var typed = ""

    effect(@mount {
        typed = default
        log.push("{label}={typed}")
    })
    ui.text(value="{label}: {typed}")
}

component app ui.node {
    var labels = ["a", "b"]

    ui.vbox {
        for var label = labels {
            field(label=label, default="none")
        }
    }
}

func testEachCopyStartsFromItsDefault(t test.Test, c app) {
    t.assert(log.join(",") == "a=none,b=none")
}
